summary: A responsive corporate banking web app inspired by the workflow breadth of Nepal products BizNex and CorporatePay, with an operations dashboard as the first screen. Branding, copy, and visual assets will be original.

questions.question: Which language should the web dashboard use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed React application with a maintainable component and data-contract layer.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: React application using JavaScript without static type checking.

questions.rationale: TypeScript is the strongest default for a multi-page banking operations interface with shared API contracts.

questions.question: Which frontend framework and rendering approach should the dashboard use?

options.label: React with Vite
options.description: Fast client-side dashboard development with a straightforward Node.js API integration.

options.label: Next.js
options.description: React framework with routing, server rendering, and a larger full-stack surface.

options.label: Vue with Vite
options.description: Component-based dashboard using Vue and its ecosystem.

questions.rationale: React with Vite keeps an empty-workspace prototype focused while leaving the Node.js API independently deployable.

questions.question: Which dashboard capabilities are essential for the first implementation?
questions.recommendedChoice: Operations dashboard with accounts, payments, approvals, beneficiaries, reports, notifications, and audit activity
questions.answer: Operations dashboard with accounts, payments, approvals, beneficiaries, reports, notifications, and audit activity
questions.rationale: The requested corporate banking direction calls for an operational first screen rather than a marketing landing page.

questions.question: Which language should the banking API use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Node.js API with typed request, response, and domain models.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Node.js API using JavaScript without static type checking.

questions.rationale: TypeScript satisfies the explicit Node.js requirement while reducing contract mistakes across banking workflows.

questions.question: Which Node.js API framework should power the banking operations endpoints?

options.label: Fastify
options.description: Low-overhead Node.js HTTP framework with schema-friendly validation and plugins.

options.label: NestJS
options.description: Structured TypeScript framework with modules, dependency injection, and decorators.

options.label: Express
options.description: Widely adopted minimal Node.js HTTP framework with a broad middleware ecosystem.

questions.rationale: Fastify provides a lean API foundation for a dashboard prototype while leaving room for validation, auth, and audit plugins.

questions.question: Which backend scope should be planned for the prototype?
questions.recommendedChoice: Mocked banking data with production-shaped REST endpoints and role-aware approval flows
questions.answer: Mocked banking data with production-shaped REST endpoints and role-aware approval flows
questions.rationale: The request is for a plan and no live bank integration or credentials are available in the empty workspace.

sharedQuestions.question: Which data stores should the project plan include?

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational store for organizations, accounts, payments, approvals, beneficiaries, and audit records.

options.label: Redis
options.description: Optional cache and short-lived session or rate-limit state.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use in-memory mocked data only for a static prototype.

sharedQuestions.rationale: Corporate banking workflows need relational consistency and auditable records; Redis is not required for the initial plan.

sharedQuestions.question: Should users sign in to access application API features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Include a sign-in boundary and role-aware access for banking operations.

options.label: No
options.description: Keep the prototype API publicly accessible within the local development environment.

sharedQuestions.rationale: Payment initiation, approvals, and audit activity should be represented as authenticated operations even with mocked data.
